moriath_0.m: Hello. It's so very long since I have seen another person. Who are you, and why are you here?
r: I'm $playername. I'm looking for my brother, Andor. Have you seen him?

moriath_1.m: No. I just told you that you are the first person I have seen here in a very long time. Getting to the old manor is difficult and dangerous, and there is nothing here. So why would anyone come here?
r: I guess I'll be going then.

Finally, success. I had to raise the spirits of many family members, but Jerelin said he would release you from the oath. There is one condition though. You must move his grave away from that of his wife. They don't seem to get along very well.
Audela told me to talk again to her husband Jerelin. I think I don't need another of Jerelin's items again. His seal should still be enough.
Cuned now sent me to his mother Audela. Where are Audela's item?
Jerelin was not helpful. In fact, he just ignored me.
Cuned has sent me to talk to his father Jerelin. Now I need a personal item of him
I spoke to the spirit of Eyvipa. Even now he was extremely displeased at being passed over in favor of Cuned in the line of succession. Do you know where I might find a personal item of him?
I spoke to the spirit of Verigil, but he told me he cannot help. I must speak to his uncle, Eyvipa. So I need a personal item of his. Do you know where I might find one?
I have found how to raise a spirit and talk to it. However, I need a personal item from the deceased.
Can you tell me about this place?
Can you tell me again why you are still here?
I have to leave to look for my brother.

moriath_1_1.m: Well, the previous lord was Verigil. His son, Adakin, did not take any of his fathers possesions when he left. You might find something in the master bedroom.

moriath_2_1.m: There are items from all the generations scattered around. They were fond of putting their intials on them. A mixture of vanity and possessiveness I think. So see if you can find something with "E" marked on it.

moriath_3_1.m: Cuned has put a "C" as intials on his personal items. Please look for it yourself.

moriath_4_1.m: Jerelin has put a "J" as intials on his personal items. Please look for it yourself.

moriath_5_1.m: Maybe it helps if you talk to Cuned again?

moriath_6_1.m: Audela has always an "A" as intials on her personal items. They should be easy to find.

moriath_9_1.m: Thank you. I will do that if it releases me from the oath. I will do it immediately. Farewell, and thanks again.

moriath_caretaker_1.m: I am Moriath, the caretaker for this manor.
r: Can you tell me more about this place?
If there is nobody else here, why do you stay?

moriath_caretaker_2.m:
I am bound by an oath to take care of the manor. It is not an oath I ever gave though. 

I cannot care for everything of course. I take care of the main house, the bridges, and tend to the graves as best I can. Everything else has gradually fallen to ruin.
r: How can you be bound by an oath you never gave?

moriath_caretaker_3.m: It is a matter of honor. The Lord of the manor saved my great-great grandfather from certain death many years ago. In return my great-great grandfather vowed that his family would always look after the manor.
r: He should not have made a vow that bound his family for generations!
Well, that's too bad for you. I need to get going. I have to find my brother.

moriath_caretaker_4.m: I do not disagree, but he did.
r: Is there something I can do to help?
Too bad. Look on the bright side though. You have an entire manor to yourself. Bye.

moriath_caretaker_5.m: The only thing that would help is for me to be released from the oath.

moriath_caretaker_6.m: The current lord, of course. But he has gone. I do not know his whereabouts, or even if he is still alive. If I knew he was deceased I would consider the oath void, but I do not know that.

moriath_caretaker_7.m: Any of the past lords Laeroth could release me from the oath. But, like my great-great grandfather, they are long dead. Their graves are in the tomb on the far island. So unless you can talk to the dead, they will be of no help.
r: How can I talk to the dead?

moriath_caretaker_8.m: I have no idea. I am a caretaker, not a priest. The manor has an extensive library. Maybe you should look there.
r: That sounds like a lot of work, and I need to go and find my brother.

moriath_history_1.m: This is Laeroth manor. Or what is left of it, anyway.
r: Can you tell me more about this place?

moriath_history_3.m: Many years ago, this island was used as a refuge in times of danger by communities that lived on the lakeshore. There was little here other than a small fortification, but being an island, that was enough for protection.

moriath_history_4.m: Then a man by the name of Laeroth, along with a group of followers, declared himself the Lord of Laeroth, and took the fortifications and the island as his own.

moriath_history_5.m:
For many years his family continued to provide refuge to those that lived on the shore, and they even built a watchtower on the mountain to the south, as a lookout for approaching enemies.
In return, the manor was provided with supplies.
r: Maybe I shouldn't have asked. This is getting boring. I need to leave, and look for my brother.

moriath_history_6.m: The fall of the manor began when the shore folk, led by a man called Korhald, built a bridge to an island, and founded the city of Remgard.

moriath_history_6a.m: They admired Korhald because without him the city of Remgard would not exist, but he was not well liked. He ruled the city like an oppressive king. When he died the cityfolk built a tomb in his honor, but well away from Remgard. Somewhere to the south.

moriath_history_7.m: Anyway, Remgard was far from any enemies, and easily defended, so the islands in the lake were no longer important, and the supplies stopped coming.

moriath_history_8.m: With no place to grow food on the islands most of the staff left. The last lord that resided here had only one son, and when the lord died his son abandoned the manor and left to look for other opportunities.
r: So if the son has left, why do you stay here?
Thanks for the history lesson. I need to leave, and look for my brother.

laeroth_nondisplay.13: Raised the spirit of cuned again
laeroth_nondisplay.102: Inside the Laeroth barn basement, the PC has found the Mystery Laeroth key.
laeroth_nondisplay.103: This is just a wrapper around the odd coin collector 65 and 66 steps, it is easier to check this one when looking for confirmation that the PC found the Coin of Prestige and the Shield of the Brave.
laeroth_nondisplay.104: The PC has helped heal Forenza. This is just a wrapper around the odd coin collector quest's "aid" Forenza steps.
laeroth_nondisplay.105: I gave Gylew the Korhald chest.
laeroth_nondisplay.106: This is just a wrapper around the odd coin collector "end" steps as there are 4 of them, it is easier to check this one when looking for confirmation that the quest is complete.
laeroth_nondisplay.107: Sold 5 bronze and 5 silver coins to the coin collector.

laeroth_caretaker.10: I met a caretaker at Laeroth manor. He said he cannot leave because he is bound by an oath, but not one he ever gave.
laeroth_caretaker.15: The caretaker said that he feels honor bound by a pledge that his great-great grandfather made many years ago.
laeroth_caretaker.17: Moriath told me only the past lords can release him from the oath, but they are dead. He suggested I look in the library for information about how to talk to them.
laeroth_caretaker.20: I have learned the chant needed to send spirits back to their rest on the other side.
laeroth_caretaker.30: I have learned how to raise the spirits of the dead with the help of an oegyth crystal. But I also need a personal item. I should talk to Moriath again.
laeroth_caretaker.35: Moriath suggested I search the master bedroom for a personal item from the last lord, Verigil.
laeroth_caretaker.40: Verigil told me he could not release the Caretaker from his oath, because he is from the wrong branch of the family. I must talk to his uncle, Eyvipa. He has gone back to his rest.
laeroth_caretaker.50: Moriath suggested I look for an item with "E" engraved on it. This would have belonged to Eyvipa.
laeroth_caretaker.60: I have found an expensive looking candlestick with "E" engraved on it. This must have belonged to Eyvipa.
laeroth_caretaker.70: Eyvipa was angry that I woke him from his rest. He refused to help me because his father passed him over, and made his younger brother, Cuned, lord. I had to send him back to his rest with the chant "estray inyay eacepay".
laeroth_caretaker.80: I found a diary that must have belonged to Cuned.
laeroth_caretaker.90: Cuned told me that Verigil is correct, and he cannot release the caretaker from his oath because he is from the wrong branch of the family. I must talk to his father, Jerelin.
laeroth_caretaker.100: After much searching I found a seal for Jerelin in an old chest. I must go back to the tomb again.
laeroth_caretaker.110: Jerelin ignored me, and went back to his resting place. I will have to ask Cuned again what to do.
laeroth_caretaker.120: Cuned told me to speak to his mother, Audela. Jerelin didn't listen to many people, but he listened to her.
laeroth_caretaker.130: I have found what appears to be a jewelry box, with "A" inscribed on it. It is locked though, and too heavy to move to the tomb.
laeroth_caretaker.140: I have found a key in the bedroom.
laeroth_caretaker.150: The key fitted the jewelry box! Inside I found a necklace "With love to Audela" written on the back.
laeroth_caretaker.160: Audela told me to talk to Jerelin again, but tell him Audela wants this done.
laeroth_caretaker.170: I spoke to Jerelin again, and told him of Audela's wishes. He told me he will release the caretaker, but with a condition. The caretakers last act must be to move his grave away from that of his nagging wife.
laeroth_caretaker.180: I told the caretaker what he has to do to be released from the oath. He thanked me, and agreed to do it.
